groups.label: Genesis of Guardians and Tales
groups.summary: The emergence of the luxurious state necessitates war and dedicated guardians whose nature must unite spirit with gentleness. In training these guardians from youth, strict censorship is established over poets to exclude harmful myths of divine strife.
groups.rationale: Consecutive passages in Book II tracing the foundation of the guardian class from the luxurious state to their moral education.

groups.label: Judicial and Ruling Authority
groups.summary: Socrates establishes that judicial knowledge must come from late observation rather than early exposure to evil, and specifies that elder guardians dedicated to the public good are chosen to rule.
groups.rationale: Passages from Book III detailing the qualifications, character preservation, and selection of judicial and governing leaders.

groups.label: Book V Proposals and Philosophy
groups.summary: Following an interruption demanding an account of the community of wives and children, Socrates asserts equal education and duties for women, sets limits on inter-Hellenic warfare, and defines true philosophers as lovers of the vision of truth.
groups.rationale: A thematic sequence of discussions spanning Book V on radical societal proposals, warfare conduct, and the nature of the philosopher.

groups.label: Pleasures of Smell Example
groups.summary: The sensation of scent is provided as an instance of pure pleasure that arises without prior suffering or deficit and departs without pain.
groups.rationale: An isolated Book IX philosophical analysis of pleasure that stands apart from the surrounding political, educational, and paratextual themes.

groups.label: Index: Concepts of the Republic
groups.summary: Editorial index entries comprehensively catalog citations concerning the qualifications of guardians, critiques of mimetic poetry and Homer, the definitions of philosophers and rulers, and the nature of the state and virtue.
groups.rationale: A cohesive block of paratextual subject index entries surveying the Republic's major philosophical and civic concepts.

groups.label: Transcriber Editorial Notes
groups.summary: Editorial notes provide documentation of typographic corrections, collation details, and the structural markup used for marginal Stephanus numbers and Greek transliteration.
groups.rationale: A standalone technical apparatus note explaining transcription standards, typography, and Greek transliteration.
